title: SARS-CoV-2 Genomic Variation - African Perspective
author: Olabode Omotoso
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bmpfk5jn

steps.title: Mine SARS-CoV-2 Genomic Sequences
steps.instruction: Extract SARS-CoV-2 genomic sequences from the GISAID database (epicov.org) using specific filters.

substeps.instruction: Filter sequences by 'high coverage only, Homo sapiens, complete, all clades and low coverage excl'

steps.title: Collect Patient and Demographic Data
steps.instruction: Gather patient and population data to determine age distribution and prevalence.

substeps.instruction: Obtain the patient's age for all mined sequences
Obtain the age distribution of countries with the highest COVID-19 prevalence from the World Factbook (www.cia.gov)

steps.title: Collect Country-Level Epidemiological Data
steps.instruction: Retrieve COVID-19 statistics and population data from Worldometer (worldometers.info) and the WHO database (covid19.who.int).

substeps.instruction: Obtain the number of confirmed cases, recoveries, and reported deaths per country
Obtain the number of tests performed per country

steps.title: Analyze Genomic Variability and Evolution
steps.instruction: Analyze the mined viral sequences and use the GISAID web interface to evaluate the outbreak's evolution.

substeps.instruction: Analyze genomic variability from the index case in Africa (February 2020) to identify mutation frequency and spread in the African population
Evaluate transmission in mutational hotspots on the GISAID interface, focusing on recurrent mutations likely to promote higher transmission rates

steps.title: Calculate Epidemiological Rates
steps.instruction: Calculate the testing, fatality, and recovery rates for each African country using the collected data.

substeps.instruction: Calculate Testing Rate (%) = (Total COVID-19 tests done / Country's population) x 100
Calculate Fatality Rate (%) = (Total number of COVID-19 deaths reported / Number of confirmed cases) x 100
Calculate Recovery Rate (%) = (Total number of COVID-19 infected patients who recovered / Number of confirmed cases) x 100
